lines.text: Scotland's national animal is a unicorn.
Not a lion. Not a stag. And wait till you see the chains.
Scottish kings put unicorns on their royal coat of arms.
They even made a gold coin called the unicorn, first struck in fourteen eighty-four.
lines.caption: They even made a gold coin called the unicorn, first struck in 1484.

lines.text: In Celtic legend, the unicorn stood for purity and power.
So why the golden chains? It's thought only a Scottish king could tame one.
Since sixteen oh three, it has stood beside the English lion on the royal arms.
lines.caption: Since 1603, it has stood beside the English lion on the royal arms.

lines.text: Sounds fake? It's true. Follow for more.
